newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela April inflation rises to 2.4 percent.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela April inflation rises to 2.4 percent.

text.p: Consumer prices in Venezuela rose 2.4 percent in April, down from 8.6 percent in April 1996 but up from 1.6 percent in March, the Venezuelan Central Bank said.
Cumulative inflation for the last 12 months was 64.9 percent, compared to 85.8 percent in the year to April 1996, the bank said.
It was the first rise in the monthly inflation rate in six months. March's inflation rate of 1.6 percent was the lowest in five years.
The acceleration of price rises to 2.4 percent in April was roughly in line with market expectations following a 70 percent rise in public sector wages in mid-February.
Cumulative inflation for the first four months of 1997 was 9.1 percent, compared to 34.5 percent in the same period last year, the bank statement showed.
The bank attributed April's price rises principally to higher prices for foodstuffs due to seasonal factors and authorized increases in public services such as gas and telephones.

According to the Central Bank, which measures the indicator based on a survey of prices in a broad range of goods and services in the capital, prices of "Food, drinks and tobacco" rose 3.1 percent in April.
The category "Household expenditures" rose 2.5 percent, "Various expenditures," 1.8 percent and "Shoes and clothing," 1.3 percent.
The government has set a target of bringing annual inflation down from 103.2 percent in 1996 to about 30 percent this year.
But local and international analysts have warned that wage pressures and a lack of control over fiscal accounts could jeopardize that goal.
